\begin{lemma}[Integrability of a Gaussian density product]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_standardGaussianPDF_mul}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_standardGaussianPDF_mul}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianPDF}
\difficulty{3}
If $u:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ is integrable under the standard Gaussian probability
measure $\gamma$, then the function $x\mapsto\varphi(x)u(x)$ is integrable with respect
to Lebesgue measure, where $\varphi$ is the standard Gaussian density.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Gaussian integral over a half-line]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_Iic_standardGaussianMeasure}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_Iic_standardGaussianMeasure}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianPDF}
\difficulty{4}
For every function $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ and every $t\in\mathbb R$, its integral
over $(-\infty,t]$ with respect to the standard Gaussian measure equals its Lebesgue
integral over that interval weighted by the standard Gaussian density $\varphi$:
\[\int_{(-\infty,t]} f\,d\gamma=\int_{(-\infty,t]}\varphi(x)f(x)\,dx.\]
\end{lemma}
